cim_eredeti: Bandwidth: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
szoveg_eredeti:
Bandwidth signed 11 customer deals over $1 million in contract value.

Third-quarter revenue reached $234 million, up 22% year over year.

Software services' annual recurring revenue exceeded $30 million.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 29, 2026, Bandwidth(NASDAQ:BAND) reported record revenue of $234 million. For long-term investors, the company demonstrated that its global network infrastructure positions it to capture growing demand as businesses adopt voice artificial intelligence. Three things management said stand out.

Enterprise contract wins give the company predictable multiyear revenue as large customers deploy services in phases. Management tracks annual contract value (ACV) to measure the annual recurring value of these customer commitments.

By owning its global telecommunications network, the business monetizes call volume rather than software seats and avoids computing fees for artificial intelligence (AI) model inference. Bandwidth refers to conversational voice AI as super intelligence, or SI, which increases call volume across its network.

Integration partnerships allow enterprise clients to use bring-your-own-carrier, or BYOC, models that connect existing telecom providers directly to cloud software. Software services, including Maestro, Bandwidth's visual software orchestration layer for routing voice workflows, exited the quarter at over $30 million in annual recurring revenue, or ARR.

Operational execution is expanding profitability alongside top-line growth. Adjusted EBITDA, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, rose 43% year over year as operating leverage took hold. Management is focusing on network reliability, international regulatory compliance, and pricing discipline to capture growing voice volume.

Management expects Enterprise Voice growth to compound over the coming quarters, driven by expanding customer contracts and network usage.
